newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby soymeal down on fund sales, oil up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby soymeal down on fund sales, oil up.

text.p: CBOT nearby soymeal futures were down sharply at midsession Monday in response to heavy commodity fund selling, CBOT floor traders said.
Soyoil futures climbed higher on talk of demand for vegetable oil in world export markets, traders said.
Refco, Rosenthall Collins, Smith Barney and R.J. O'Brien were all heavy sellers of nearby soymeal, pit traders said.
The selling was said to be linked to fund activity and pushed July soymeal down as much as $6.20 per ton earlier.
Soyoil futures stayed firm on talk of heavy to moderate buying in South American vegetable oil markets, traders said.
A commercial firm was rumored to have purchased up to 60,000 tonnes of soyoil in South American spot markets to cover business to China or Iran, U.S. export sources said.
However, no confirmation of the deal could be obtained.
Floor traders cited soyoil/soymeal spread trading as another source of strength in CBOT soyoil futures.
At 1120 CDT, soymeal was up $1.20 to down $3.00 per ton, with July down $3.70 at $269.80. Soyoil was 0.12 to 0.20 cent per lb higher, with July up 0.11 cent at 24.93 cents.
